solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Glorious adult joke captured by microphone

indicators.note: the adult joke is held within the microphone's letters, as if caught on it

parts.note: MIC is the short form of microphone
A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult
a jest is a joke

explanation.surface: A splendid bit of grown-up humour gets recorded on a mic.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something magnificent and splendid in its grandeur.

clue.text: Don't forget to ditch repulsive, gutless parliamentarian

indicators.note: ditching means throwing away, so the next letters are removed from the reminder word

parts.note: to remember is not to forget

indicators.note: with its guts removed, only the outside letters of repulsive remain

explanation.surface: A reminder to get rid of an odious, spineless MP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutless' leaves RE, the outer letters of repulsive, and 'to ditch' takes RE from REMEMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: An MP is a Member of Parliament, so a parliamentarian is a member.

clue.text: Stone me, she gets about in style!

parts.note: jet is a black stone used in jewellery
the crossword's compiler, the setter, speaking of herself as me

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at a woman who travels glamorously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone me' looks like the British exclamation of astonishment, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the wealthy, fashionable set who fly around the world, travelling in luxury.

clue.text: Swimmer beginning to soap buttocks

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, here of soap

parts.note: prat is an old British slang word for the buttocks

explanation.surface: Someone in the pool starts lathering their backside.
explanation.definitionFit: The sprat is a small fish, so it is an example of a swimmer.

clue.text: Work — tire — eat — repeat.

indicators.note: to work letters is to knead them into a new shape, so tire and eat are rearranged

explanation.surface: The grind of daily life: work, get tired, eat, and do it all again.
explanation.definitionFit: To say or do something over again is a synonym of to repeat.

clue.text: One suffering grimly at heart after winner loses gold

indicators.note: the heart of grimly is placed after the shortened winner
to lose something is to go without it, so the gold is taken away

parts.note: a victor is a winner
OR is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, here the centre two letters of grimly

explanation.surface: Someone who suffers terribly once a champion is stripped of their gold medal.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who suffers harm or misfortune is a victim.

clue.text: Perhaps supporting sick friend in a way the law forbids

definitions.text: in a way the law forbids

indicators.note: in a down answer a supporting piece sits below, so the example abbreviation goes under the sick piece

parts.note: ill means sick
EG (for example) signals perhaps
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Perhaps helping out an ill pal breaks the law somehow.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something unlawfully, against the law, is acting illegally.

clue.text: Oddly send up sincerest youngsters

indicators.note: in a down answer sending letters up reverses them
taking the odd-numbered letters of sincerest, first, third and so on

explanation.surface: Strangely, teasing the most earnest of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' picks SNEET from sincerest; 'send up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Young people aged thirteen to nineteen are teens, a fair synonym for youngsters.

clue.text: Optimism at Chequers disguising conflict

indicators.note: the phrase disguises a word lying across its letters

explanation.surface: Cheerful hopes at the PM's country retreat mask a clash.
explanation.walkthrough: Chequers is the British Prime Minister's country house.
explanation.definitionFit: A mismatch is a clash between things that do not agree, a conflict.

clue.text: Ship's officer hands round case of impressive military equipment

parts.note: a mate is an officer on a merchant ship

indicators.note: the two hands go round the casing of impressive

parts.note: R and L stand for the right and left hands

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside letters

explanation.surface: A ship's officer passes round a crate of splendid army kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' gives IE from impressive, and 'round' puts it between R and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Materiel is the stock of weapons, supplies and equipment used by armed forces.

clue.text: Walks on water across lake, gripping tool

indicators.note: the piers stretch across the lake, enclosing its abbreviation

parts.note: piers are walkways built out over water

explanation.surface: A miracle-worker strides across a lake holding an implement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walks on water' wants to be a miracle; it is jetties over the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliers are a hand implement with jaws for holding things tightly.

clue.text: Balearic port cut lifeline here

indicators.note: cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: Palma is the capital and port of Majorca, in the Balearic Islands

explanation.surface: A Mediterranean harbour has its lifeline severed.
explanation.definitionFit: Palmistry reads the lifeline as a crease on the hand, so that is where it is found.

clue.text: Standing up in court after regularly ignoring decree

indicators.note: the court abbreviation comes after the kept letters
ignoring every other letter of decree, keeping the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: Someone rises in court after repeatedly disregarding a ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly ignoring' drops D, C and E from decree, leaving ERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something upright and vertical is described as standing up.

clue.text: Performing seal again feeling no pain

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters do tricks, rearranging themselves

explanation.surface: A circus seal goes on stage once more, untroubled by aches.
explanation.definitionFit: Analgesia is the medical term for insensibility to pain.

clue.text: Small store struggled

parts.note: a trove is a hoard or store, as in treasure trove

explanation.surface: A little shop had a hard time.
explanation.definitionFit: Strove is the past tense of strive, to make great efforts, so it means struggled.

clue.text: Unscented old roses lead to unusual stir

indicators.note: stirring mixes the letters up
the lead of a word is its first letter, here of unusual

explanation.surface: Antique roses give rise to an odd commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead to' gives U, the first letter of unusual, which 'stir' mixes with OLDROSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no smell or scent is odourless.

clue.text: Camel, if ill-treated, causing destruction

indicators.note: letters that are ill-treated are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: An abused camel may turn destructive.
explanation.definitionFit: Malefic is a literary word for harmful, doing evil or mischief.

clue.text: Mad gerbil fan liable to go to pieces

indicators.note: mad letters run wild into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A crazed gerbil enthusiast is on the verge of breakdown.
explanation.definitionFit: Frangible means brittle or easily broken, so liable to shatter.

clue.text: Barmen stripped after women's party got livelier

indicators.note: the stripped barmen come after the women's letter

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women

indicators.note: stripped of its outer letters, keeping the middle of barmen

parts.note: the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A hen night turned lively once the bar staff took their clothes off.
explanation.definitionFit: To warm up is an idiom for becoming more lively or animated.

clue.text: Bearing wine for Charles de Gaulle?

parts.note: an air is a person's bearing or manner
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A grand manner and a glass of wine suit the French general.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows the definition is an example: Charles de Gaulle is the main Paris airport.
explanation.definitionFit: The French statesman gave his name to the Paris hub for flights, an example of the kind.

clue.text: Thin, ugly, half-cut brute

indicators.note: each word is cut in half, keeping its front half

explanation.surface: A skinny, ugly, rather drunk ruffian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' is British slang for drunk, but here it keeps TH and UG.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent, brutish person, a ruffian, is a thug.

clue.text: They'd a yearning to preserve golden age

indicators.note: the phrase preserves a word within its run of letters

explanation.surface: People longed to keep a past era of glory.
explanation.definitionFit: One's heyday is the time of greatest success, a peak period.

clue.text: Impetuous type roasting nut

parts.note: roasting means very hot
nut is slang for head

explanation.surface: A rash person chestnut-roasting by the fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash, quick-tempered person who acts without thinking is a hothead.

clue.text: Extremely sexy nurses rent floor of building

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the outer letters cradle the torn piece
the extremes of sexy are its first and last letters

parts.note: rent, as a past tense, means tore

explanation.surface: Very attractive nurses pay rent on a level of the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like a payment, but it is the past of rend.
explanation.definitionFit: A storey is one level or floor of a building.

clue.text: Unimportant match for clubs?

parts.note: minor means unimportant
to suit is to match

explanation.surface: A trivial game laid on for sports clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, clubs and diamonds rank lower than hearts and spades.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge clubs is one of the two lower-ranking card suits, hence an example.

clue.text: One had an upset on river bottom

indicators.note: in a down answer the upturned letters sit on top of the river
in a down answer upset means turned upside down, so read upwards

parts.note: I'D is short for I had, one person having

explanation.surface: Someone capsized on a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point, the very bottom.

clue.text: After cycling, entered bar

indicators.note: cycling moves letters round from one end to the other

parts.note: got in means entered

explanation.surface: Following a bike ride, someone walked into a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves GOT from the front of GOTIN to the end. 'bar' looks like a pub; it is a block of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a block or bar of cast metal, such as gold.

clue.text: Archetypal males leaving mid- meal

indicators.note: the males leave, so their letters are taken out

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male, so two of them is MM

explanation.surface: Men walking out halfway through dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'mid- meal' are used as printed; removing both Ms leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Archetypal means being a perfect model or typical example of something.

clue.text: Stranger following driver's initial progress uncertainly

indicators.note: the stranger piece follows the driver's initial
the initial of a word is its first letter

parts.note: odder means stranger

explanation.surface: A weird person tails a learner motorist creeping along.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodder is to totter or move shakily, as an old person might.

clue.text: Glower after Washington restricts Ecstasy for 31 days

indicators.note: the glower comes after the capital piece
the capital's letters hem in the drug's

parts.note: Washington DC is the US capital
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
something that glows, a glower, is an ember

explanation.surface: A scowl as the US capital clamps down on a drug for a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glower' looks like a scowl but is read as glow-er, one that glows.
explanation.definitionFit: The final month of the year has thirty-one days.

clue.text: Pass away — for each is, primarily, human

parts.note: per means for each

indicators.note: primarily means first, so the first letter of human

explanation.surface: A reflection that every person must die, being primarily human.
explanation.definitionFit: To perish is to die, a synonym for passing away.

clue.text: Dissolute sinner excluded from unrestrainedly wild, illicit sex

indicators.note: dissolute signals the sinner's letters are loose, not in order
the sinner's letters are taken out of the long word
wild means the remaining letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A debauched sinner is barred from unbridled illicit sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excluded from' takes the letters of sinner out of unrestrainedly, and 'wild' rearranges the remaining UTRAEDLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sex outside marriage by a married person is adultery, a kind of illicit sex.
